context:
Patient: 62M, ECOG 1, with 3 months of enlarging left neck nodes, fevers, drenching night sweats and 7 kg weight loss; PET-CT shows cervical, mediastinal and an 11 cm retroperitoneal mass, plus splenomegaly with FDG-avid splenic lesions; marrow negative, LDH 735 (about 3x ULN), LVEF 58%. Node biopsy: DLBCL NOS, non-GCB by Hans, MYC 50% / BCL2 80% by IHC with FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements; HBsAg nonreactive, anti-HBc reactive, anti-HBs reactive.
What this case tests: Spleen involvement is nodal (lymphatic) under Lugano, so the stage is III, not IV, and the spleen does not score as extranodal in IPI or CNS-IPI. | MYC/BCL2 protein co-expression without rearrangement is double-expressor, not double-hit, and does not justify DA-EPOCH-R. | HBsAg-negative but anti-HBc-positive serology is resolved hepatitis B: rituximab needs entecavir or tenofovir prophylaxis started before the first dose. | CNS-IPI 3 is intermediate risk with no high-risk sites or neurologic symptoms, so routine CNS prophylaxis, MRI brain and lumbar puncture are not indicated. | A fit 62-year-old with ECOG 1 who wants cure gets full-dose curative therapy, not dose-reduced or palliative treatment.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, newly diagnosed (first presentation, no prior lymphoma). Excisional biopsy of left cervical level IV lymph node collected 2026-09-09; final pathology with FISH addendum 2026-09-16. Non-germinal-center B-cell phenotype by Hans algorithm (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive in about 70%). CD20 strongly positive, PAX5 positive, CD3 negative in tumor cells, CD5 negative, CD10 negative, CD30 negative, cyclin D1 negative, EBER negative. Ki-67 about 85%. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (2026-09-10) show no lymphoma involvement. Coding note: the problem list uses ICD-10-CM C83.30 (unspecified site); this is nodal disease at multiple sites, so C83.38 is the more accurate code.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IV-B with bulky disease (provisional, see note). Nodal disease above the diaphragm (left cervical levels III-IV up to 3.1 cm, right paratracheal node 2.6 cm, subcarinal node 2.2 cm) and below it (left para-aortic and aortocaval retroperitoneal mass 11.0 x 8.1 cm, SUVmax 22.4, bulky at 10 cm or more). Multifocal FDG-avid splenic lesions (SUVmax up to 16.3) in an enlarged 14.2 cm spleen (PET-CT 2026-09-05; spleen tip palpable on exam). Bone marrow negative. Liver, lungs, bones, adrenals and kidneys not involved on PET. B symptoms present: fevers to 38.5 C several times a week and drenching night sweats. Weight loss is 8.1% (86 to 79 kg; 78.4 kg on 2026-09-17), below the 10% criterion, but fever and sweats alone meet B. Note: strict Ann Arbor treats the spleen as a lymphatic (nodal) organ, which would make this III-S B; I am counting the multifocal splenic lesions as stage IV, as the PET read does. Either way the IPI stage point is the same (III and IV both score 1) and the regimen is the same, so the decision does not depend on this.
answer.biology: Non-GCB (activated B-cell-like by IHC) DLBCL with a double-expressor phenotype: MYC protein in about 50% and BCL2 protein in about 80% of tumor cells (usual cutoffs MYC 40% or more, BCL2 50% or more). High proliferation (Ki-67 about 85%). Interphase break-apart FISH (200 nuclei) shows no MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21) or BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement, so this is not double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma. Flow cytometry: lambda-restricted CD19+ CD20+ B cells, CD5 and CD10 negative. Cytogenetics was submitted with the biopsy but no result is in the record. Gene-expression cell-of-origin and LymphGen genetic subtype (MYD88, CD79B, etc.) are not available. EBV negative in tissue. Implications: non-GCB and double-expressor biology, with high Ki-67, are adverse prognostic features. Without double-hit genetics, NCCN does not require DA-EPOCH-R, and R-CHOP-type therapy remains standard. Clinical trial enrollment is a reasonable alternative to discuss given the adverse biology.
answer.prognosis: Intermediate-high to high risk. IPI is 3 (age 62: 1; LDH above ULN: 1; stage IV: 1; ECOG 1: 0; extranodal sites: 0), which is high-intermediate. NCCN-IPI is likely in the high-risk group (age 61 to 75, raised LDH, beta-2 microglobulin 3.4 mg/L), but the exact points need the LDH upper limit of normal, which is not in the record. Other adverse features: 11 cm bulk, B symptoms, splenic involvement, non-GCB and double-expressor biology, Ki-67 85%, and LDH rising from 680 to 735 U/L. Favorable features: no double-hit genetics, marrow negative, no CNS or other extranodal organ involvement, ECOG 1, normal renal and hepatic function, LVEF 58%. With R-CHOP-type therapy, about 60 to 70% of patients with this IPI are expected to be alive and progression-free long term in trial populations; individual risk is uncertain. In POLARIX, pola-R-CHP improved 2-year PFS to 76.7% versus 70.2% with R-CHOP, with the benefit concentrated in intermediate-high and high IPI. The end-of-treatment PET is likely to be the strongest individual predictor, and I will use it to guide any further treatment.
answer.first_line_treatment: Curative-intent first-line therapy: polatuzumab vedotin plus rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and prednisone (pola-R-CHP), 6 cycles every 21 days on the POLARIX schedule, with intrathecal CNS prophylaxis as described below. Doses by BSA 1.98 m2 and weight 79 kg: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 740 mg); cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 1,485 mg); doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 99 mg); polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV day 1 (about 142 mg); prednisone 100 mg PO days 1 to 5. Vincristine is omitted, as in pola-R-CHP. Cumulative doxorubicin reaches 300 mg/m2 at cycle 6, which is the usual ceiling, so no further anthracycline will be given. Fallback if polatuzumab is not accessible: standard R-CHOP-21 x6 with vincristine 1.4 mg IV day 1 (maximum 2 mg). Reasons for this choice: IPI high-intermediate, bulk and splenic involvement make this a high-risk patient in whom the POLARIX PFS benefit matters most; pola-R-CHP is an NCCN-listed option; he is fit for full-dose therapy (ECOG 1, eGFR 96, bilirubin 0.6, LVEF 58%, albumin 3.7). I do not recommend DA-EPOCH-R, since there is no double-hit, or a steroid pre-phase, since the TLS risk is managed with allopurinol and hydration. Start after the pre-treatment steps below, targeting C1D1 within about 1 to 2 weeks of tumor board. He has already had about 6 weeks since biopsy (2026-09-09) with no treatment, so there should be no further delay.
answer.cns_risk: CNS-IPI is 3 of 6: age over 60 (1), stage III-IV (1), LDH above ULN (1), ECOG 2 or more (0), 2 or more extranodal sites (0), kidney or adrenal involvement (0). Score 3 falls in the high-risk tier (3 to 6) of the original CNS-IPI, with a roughly 10% 2-year CNS relapse rate in the derivation cohort (a population estimate, not a patient-specific one). He has no testicular, paranasal sinus, kidney or adrenal involvement, and no double-hit genetics. Decision: offer CNS prophylaxis with intrathecal methotrexate 12 mg, on a schedule per local protocol (commonly with cycles 1 to 6, or cycles 1, 3 and 5). Before the first intrathecal dose, obtain a brain MRI with and without contrast and an LP with CSF cytology and flow cytometry to exclude occult CNS disease; CNS involvement would change therapy to high-dose methotrexate-based treatment. LP requires platelets above 50 and a normal INR and aPTT on the day. He has no neurologic symptoms and a non-focal neurologic exam. Revisit this decision if neurologic symptoms appear, if restaging shows kidney, adrenal, testicular or sinus involvement, or if the patient declines intrathecal therapy.
answer.response_assessment: Use Lugano 2014 criteria with the 5-point Deauville PET scale. Reference study: baseline FDG-PET-CT of 2026-09-05, which predates the biopsy and treatment. Deauville comparators are liver SUVmax 2.6 and mediastinal blood pool SUVmax 2.0. Target lesions for sum-of-products measurement: left cervical 3.1 x 2.4 cm, right paratracheal 2.6 cm, subcarinal 2.2 cm, retroperitoneal 11.0 x 8.1 cm (use the same CT or PET protocol each time). Interim PET-CT after cycle 2 is for information only; I will not change therapy on an interim Deauville 4 or 5 alone outside a trial. End-of-treatment PET-CT about 3 to 6 weeks after cycle 6. Target is Deauville 1 to 3, with resolution of the splenic lesions and no new lesions. Clinical and laboratory response: fevers and night sweats should resolve within about 2 to 3 cycles, and LDH and beta-2 microglobulin should normalize. Rising LDH together with new fever is a red flag for progression and should prompt early restaging. If end-of-treatment PET shows Deauville 4 or 5 at the retroperitoneal site, refer to radiation oncology for consolidative involved-site RT (about 30 Gy); biopsy first if the uptake is equivocal. Radiation is decided by the end-of-treatment PET, not by bulk alone, so no RT if the response is complete. Surveillance after treatment: clinical review and labs about every 3 months for 2 years; imaging only for symptoms or a clinical concern. If he relapses or progresses, the plan is a biopsy and referral for salvage therapy, with autologous transplant or CAR T-cell eligibility assessed then.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Before C1D1: (1) Repeat CBC with differential (last CBC was 2026-09-03; the 2026-09-16 draw was chemistry only), CMP, LDH, uric acid, phosphate and magnesium. (2) PT/INR, aPTT and fibrinogen; none are in the record, and they are needed for LP and port placement. (3) Hepatitis B: HBsAg negative, anti-HBc positive, anti-HBs positive, which is resolved infection with high reactivation risk on rituximab. Send quantitative HBV DNA and LFTs. Start entecavir 0.5 mg PO daily now, before the first rituximab dose, and continue for at least 12 months after the last rituximab dose (longer if HBV DNA is detectable). Monitor HBV DNA and ALT every 1 to 3 months during and after therapy. (4) Quantitative IgG, IgA and IgM before rituximab. (5) G6PD activity, needed before rasburicase could be used. (6) Cytogenetic (karyotype) result from the pathology lab. (7) Brain MRI with and without contrast and LP with CSF cytology and flow, before the first intrathecal methotrexate dose. (8) Implanted port placed by interventional radiology, since doxorubicin is a vesicant. (9) Echocardiogram done 2026-09-08 (LVEF 58%, GLS -20%); repeat only for cardiac symptoms, since cumulative doxorubicin is at the 300 mg/m2 ceiling. (10) Document a formal ECOG and a baseline neuropathy exam. (11) Non-live vaccines (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal conjugate, recombinant zoster) if they can be given without delaying C1; no live vaccines. (12) Offer sperm banking and document the discussion. (13) Insurance prior authorization for polatuzumab, pegfilgrastim and entecavir. (14) Informed consent covering hair loss, infection, cardiotoxicity, neuropathy, hyperglycemia, HBV, and the intrathecal methotrexate plan.
answer.supportive_care: Primary G-CSF: pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 4 of each cycle (or an on-body injector), because age over 60 with an anthracycline-cyclophosphamide regimen carries meaningful febrile neutropenia risk. Antiemetics: treat as high emetic risk (anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide): NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist and dexamethasone, with olanzapine for breakthrough nausea. Tumor lysis prophylaxis: intermediate-to-high risk (bulk 11 cm, LDH about 2.7 to 3 times ULN, uric acid 7.1 mg/dL). Start allopurinol 300 mg PO daily 1 to 2 days before C1, with oral or IV hydration as tolerated. Check K, phosphate, creatinine and uric acid at baseline and 6 to 24 hours after C1. Use rasburicase only if uric acid rises or renal function falls, and only after G6PD status is known. HBV: entecavir as above. PJP prophylaxis: TMP-SMX DS one tablet three times weekly (or single-strength daily) for the steroid period (cycles 1 to 6) and for about 1 to 2 months afterward; atovaquone if sulfa intolerance or cytopenias. Valacyclovir 500 mg BID during therapy is reasonable for HSV and VZV prophylaxis. Fever plan: check and record temperature before any acetaminophen, because his current acetaminophen use can mask fever; call the same day for temperature of 38.0 C or higher; febrile neutropenia pathway applies. Avoid NSAIDs (platelets and renal function during TLS risk). Hypothyroidism: continue levothyroxine and check TSH every 6 to 8 weeks. Steroid hyperglycemia: check glucose during prednisone days. Alopecia: discuss scalp cooling, which gives partial protection and is less effective with anthracyclines, and wig referral. Anemia (Hb 10.8): transfuse for Hb below 7 to 8 g/dL or symptoms. Nutrition: 8.8% weight loss from 86 kg; dietitian referral. Spleen 14.2 cm: avoid contact sports and teach him to report sudden left upper abdominal or shoulder pain. Retroperitoneal mass displaces the left renal vein without hydronephrosis: check creatinine each cycle and obtain renal ultrasound if it rises. Continue omeprazole and atorvastatin; neither has a meaningful interaction with the planned regimen. Limit alcohol during treatment.
answer.fitness_and_goals: He is fit for full-dose curative therapy: age 62, ECOG 1 on 2026-09-02 (still fully independent in self-care, working reduced hours, no longer hiking), normal renal and hepatic function, LVEF 58%, no diabetes, no significant comorbidity beyond treated hypothyroidism, GERD and hyperlipidemia, and no documented neuropathy. ECOG should be re-documented at C1D1. Goals (2026-09-17 note): treatment aimed at cure, continue working part-time from home, and be well for his daughter's wedding in May 2027. Timeline: C1 in late October to early November 2026 if pre-treatment work-up is done promptly; 6 cycles every 21 days end around mid-February to March 2027; end-of-treatment PET about 3 to 6 weeks later (March to April 2027); radiation, if needed, about 3 to 4 weeks after that (around April 2027). The May 2027 wedding is achievable but close, so any radiation should be scheduled around it. Work: he can keep working from home at reduced hours; expect the lowest energy and output in the days 7 to 14 nadir window after each infusion. Monthly job-site visits may be possible in the off-nadir week with infection precautions and an agreed plan for crowded or poorly ventilated sites; discuss this cycle by cycle. Provide an employer letter and leave paperwork as needed. Expected toxicities to counsel on: fatigue, alopecia, infection, cardiotoxicity (monitored by cumulative dose), hyperglycemia on steroids, and peripheral neuropathy (less with pola-R-CHP than with vincristine). No driving restriction unless fatigue or sedation affects him.
missing_information: LDH upper limit of normal from the reporting lab. Needed for exact IPI, NCCN-IPI, CNS-IPI and TLS categories; 680 and 735 U/L are above any usual ULN, but NCCN-IPI LDH points depend on the ratio to ULN (about 2.7 to 3.0 times ULN at ULN 225 to 250).
Cytogenetic (karyotype) result from the 2026-09-09 biopsy. Cytogenetics was submitted but no result is in the record, so complex karyotype or other high-risk abnormalities are unknown.
CBC with differential after 2026-09-03; no CBC was drawn on 2026-09-16.
Coagulation panel: PT/INR, aPTT and fibrinogen.
Quantitative HBV DNA and anti-HBs titer (anti-HBc and anti-HBs are reactive; no viral load in the record).
No brain MRI or CSF evaluation is documented. Needed before intrathecal methotrexate. The CNS-IPI decision assumes no occult CNS disease.
ECOG was recorded only on 2026-09-02. The 2026-09-17 note describes function but does not record a score.
Vaccination history and status (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal, recombinant zoster).
Documentation of the sperm banking discussion, and insurance coverage or prior authorization for polatuzumab, pegfilgrastim and entecavir.
The outside CT report and images from 2026-08-18 are summarized in the referral only. I used the 2026-09-05 PET-CT as the baseline study.

Date discrepancy: the chart schedules tumor board for 2026-09-18, but the current date is 2026-10-22. If the board is later than planned, repeat CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid and a focused exam before C1, reconfirm the staging, and schedule treatment urgently because aggressive lymphoma has gone untreated for about 6 weeks since biopsy.
Ferritin and iron studies: the marrow reports increased iron stores consistent with anemia of inflammation, but no ferritin value is recorded.

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not the same as the molecular activated B-cell (ABC) subtype defined by gene-expression profiling.
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III.
The response bases stage III on nodal disease above and below the diaphragm plus splenic involvement, treating the spleen as lymphatic (nodal) tissue rather than an extranodal site.
The response notes bulky disease (11 cm retroperitoneal mass, >=10 cm) and B symptoms (fevers, night sweats).
The response assigns stage IV (for example by counting the spleen as an extranodal organ).
The response counts the spleen as an extranodal site when scoring IPI or CNS-IPI.
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor (MYC 50% >=40%, BCL2 80% >=50% by IHC) but NOT double-hit (FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response states the lymphoma is NOT double-expressor despite MYC 50% and BCL2 80% by IHC.
The response calculates IPI as 3 (high-intermediate risk): age >60, elevated LDH, stage III; ECOG 1 and zero extranodal sites do not score.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 3 (intermediate risk), without counting the spleen as an extranodal site.
The response recommends curative-intent full-dose immunochemotherapy with Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP for 6 cycles.
The response names Pola-R-CHP as the preferred regimen given IPI >=2 (noting the POLARIX benefit appeared greatest in non-GCB/ABC disease), with R-CHOP an acceptable alternative.
The response considers ISRT to the initially bulky site if it remains PET-positive (residual Deauville 4-5) at the end of systemic therapy.
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R or another intensified regimen on the basis of double-expressor status alone.
The response recommends a dose-reduced regimen (e.g. R-mini-CHOP) for this fit 62-year-old with ECOG 1.

The response recognizes resolved/occult hepatitis B (HBsAg negative, anti-HBc positive) with a high risk of HBV reactivation on anti-CD20 therapy, and starts antiviral prophylaxis (entecavir or tenofovir) before the first rituximab dose, continued for at least 12 months after the last dose.
The response orders a baseline quantitative HBV DNA and liver function tests and monitors them (ALT, HBV DNA) during and after therapy.
The response states that no HBV-directed action or antiviral prophylaxis is needed (e.g. because HBsAg is negative).
The response judges CNS relapse risk as intermediate and states that routine CNS prophylaxis and routine MRI brain / lumbar puncture are not indicated without neurologic symptoms or high-risk sites.
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal chemotherapy) for this intermediate-risk patient.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response says residual Deauville 4-5 uptake at end of treatment should be biopsied before changing therapy when it would change management.
The response recognizes at least intermediate tumor-lysis risk (11 cm mass, LDH ~3x ULN) and orders allopurinol plus hydration (with TLS lab monitoring).
The response considers primary G-CSF prophylaxis (e.g. pegfilgrastim) as reasonable with this regimen.
The response notes the baseline LVEF of 58% permits anthracycline.
The response judges the patient fit for full-dose curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function, controlled comorbidities) in line with his goal of cure.
The response lists the quantitative HBV DNA level as missing information still needed.
